channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans Six-Month Ban on White Sugar Imports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan intends to prohibit the import of white sugar for a period of six months. This measure aims to regulate the domestic sugar market. The specific reasons and details of the ban are expected to be announced soon.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Canada Strengthen Cooperation in Geology and Resource Exploration
item.description: Uzbekistan and Canada are enhancing collaboration in geology, focusing on advanced technologies for seismic data processing and subsurface visualization. A meeting between Uzbekistan's Ministry of Mining and Geology and Canada's Thrust Belt Imaging (TBI) discussed potential partnerships in geophysics, exploration, and energy sectors.

item.title: OSCE Media Forum on Information Accuracy and Trust in Media Held in Bishkek
item.description: An OSCE media forum on information accuracy and trust in media for Central Asia took place in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Organized by the OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media, the event focused on strengthening cooperation and dialogue regarding media freedom, journalistic ethics, and ensuring information accuracy to build societal trust.

item.title: Uzbekistan Participates in Inter-Parliamentary Union Health Committee Meetings
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan attended meetings of the Inter-Parliamentary Union's Health Committee and a seminar on mental health during the 153rd Assembly. Discussions focused on reproductive health, maternal and child protection, and strengthening legislative frameworks and budget financing. International organizations participated in a dialogue on women's health and adolescent reproductive health.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Role in the CIS: 35 Years On and Future Prospects
item.description: As the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) approaches its 35th anniversary, Uzbekistan has significantly intensified its engagement since 2017, participating in all 66 areas of activity and proposing 90 initiatives, 80 of which are implemented. Uzbekistan will chair the organization in 2027, aiming to address existing challenges and tasks.

item.title: Kokshetau to Receive Natural Gas Within Three Years Via New Pipeline
item.description: Kokshetau and six districts in the Akmola region will be supplied with natural gas within three years through the 'Ishim – Astana' main pipeline. This project, extending the 'Saryarka' gas transmission system, aims to provide access to over 120,000 subscribers, potentially reaching 480,000 users.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Mandatory Digital Marking for Vegetable Oil by July 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan is proposing to introduce mandatory digital marking for vegetable oil starting July 1, 2027. A draft government resolution, open for discussion until October 24, aims to prevent illegal import, production, and sale of the product. This initiative follows similar digital marking systems implemented for tobacco, alcohol, medicines, and beverages.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks First in Central Asia in Most Powerful Countries Index
item.description: Kazakhstan has entered the top 100 most powerful countries globally, securing 34th place in an international ranking based on U.S. News & World Report research. The nation leads Central Asia, surpassing several neighbors. The ranking assesses economic and political influence, leadership, international partnerships, and military alliances.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Social Health Insurance System Prevents 234 Billion Tenge Losses
item.description: Kazakhstan's mandatory social health insurance system has prevented financial losses amounting to 234 billion tenge over nine months, according to the Ministry of Finance. Efforts to strengthen control have also led to the recovery of over 79 billion tenge illegally paid to medical service providers. New tools, including AI-based anti-fraud measures, are being used to prevent unjustified payments and ensure funds are used for medical care.

item.title: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas Postpones Parliamentary and Presidential Elections to 2027
item.description: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas has issued a decree postponing both the parliamentary and presidential elections, now scheduled to take place simultaneously on September 11, 2027. The parliamentary elections were previously set for November 28 of this year, while presidential elections were expected in early 2027. Abbas has been in power for over two decades.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Cooperation in Standardization with International Partners
item.description: Uzbekistan participated in the 20th plenary session of ISO/TC 100 in China, alongside delegations from France, Germany, and the UK. Discussions focused on international standardization, chain drive technologies, sustainable development, and greenhouse gas emissions reporting.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks 34th in Most Powerful Countries 2026 Index, Surpassing Several European and Middle Eastern Nations
item.description: Kazakhstan secured the 34th position in the Most Powerful Countries 2026 ranking by World Population Review, based on U.S. News & World Report data. The index assesses countries on economic and political influence, leadership, and alliances. Kazakhstan ranked higher than Denmark, UAE, and Norway, with China, the US, and India leading the list.

item.title: 17-Year-Old Uzbek Citizen Subjected to Violence in Turkey Repatriated Home
item.description: A 17-year-old Uzbek citizen, who was taken to Turkey under the guise of education, faced forced marriage, physical violence, and forced labor. The minor has been repatriated to Uzbekistan following intervention. The case highlights concerns about exploitation of young individuals abroad.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands Access to Mental Health Services in Polyclinics
item.description: Kazakhstan is enhancing mental healthcare accessibility by integrating services into polyclinics, with 304 primary mental health centers and offices operating nationwide. Over 874,000 outpatient visits were recorded in the first half of 2026. The country focuses on early detection, outpatient treatment, and rehabilitation, increasing daytime psychiatric beds and support for children.

item.title: New bridge under construction and airport modernization underway in Kazakhstan's Pavlodar region
item.description: Kazakhstan's Pavlodar region is developing its transport infrastructure with a new bridge over the Irtysh River and modernization of the Pavlodar Airport. The bridge, featuring an extradosed design, is 690 meters long. Airport upgrades include runway refurbishment and planned terminal expansion to boost air traffic, including international routes.

item.title: WHO Urges Enhanced Mental Health Support in Afghanistan Amidst Daily Challenges
item.description: The World Health Organization calls for greater attention to mental health care in Afghanistan, noting widespread psychological distress due to loss and daily hardships. WHO representative Dr. Edwin Ceniza Salvador stressed mental health's parity with physical health, encouraging those in distress to seek support and emphasizing community solidarity.

item.title: Attempt to Illegally Export $44,500 in Cash Uncovered in Uzbekistan
item.description: Authorities in Andijan and Bukhara, Uzbekistan, have stopped attempts to illegally export a total of $44,500 in cash. In Andijan, $34,000 was found on a driver heading to Kyrgyzstan. At Bukhara airport, $10,500 exceeding the limit was found in a passenger's hand luggage.

item.title: Kazakhstan anticipates record sunflower harvest, farmers propose import ban
item.description: Kazakhstan expects a record sunflower harvest this year, with farmers expressing concerns about potential price drops due to cheap imports from Russia. Local farmers have proposed a ban on sunflower imports to protect domestic prices. The head of Aitas Agro noted that current prices are already low, with oil plants offering less than the cost of production.

item.title: Interpol chiefs from Central Asia meet in Astana to discuss regional security
item.description: Heads of Interpol bureaus from Central Asia convened in Astana for a meeting focused on combating transnational organized crime, international wanted lists, cyber threats, and financial crimes. The meeting included delegations from eight countries and aimed to strengthen coordination among law enforcement agencies in the region. Kazakhstan shared its experience in utilizing Interpol's capabilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Included in Global Most Influential Countries Ranking
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have been ranked among the world's most powerful and influential countries for 2026, according to World Population Review. Kazakhstan secured 34th place, becoming the only Central Asian nation in the top half of the list. Uzbekistan ranked 71st, while Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan were not featured in the top 100.

item.title: ExxonMobil Blocked $5 Billion Kashagan Dispute Settlement Offer, Bloomberg Reports
item.description: ExxonMobil reportedly blocked a $5 billion settlement offer related to an environmental fine imposed on the Kashagan field operator for sulfur storage violations. According to Bloomberg sources, ExxonMobil persuaded TotalEnergies to adopt a similar stance, effectively halting the agreement. Kazakh courts had upheld the fine's legality.

item.title: Taliban Ministry of Justice Declares 250 Jareebs of Land in Mazar-e-Sharif as 'Emirati'
item.description: The Taliban Ministry of Justice announced that approximately 250 jareebs of land in Mazar-e-Sharif, Balkh province, have been designated as 'Emirati' property. A special court ruled that the land, known as 'Farm Haji Abdul Baqi and Haji Ismail,' belongs to the state. Those occupying the land are ordered to surrender it.

item.title: UN Rapporteur Richard Bennett Praises Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize Award
item.description: United Nations Special Rapporteur on human rights in Afghanistan, Richard Bennett, called the Nobel Peace Prize award to Navi Pillay an encouraging step for human rights defenders. He expressed delight and praised her long-standing efforts in justice, peace, international law, and human rights. Pillay, a South African lawyer, was recognized for her extensive work promoting peace and international law.

item.title: Children Playing with Fire Caused Fatal Astana Apartment Blaze, Ministry Reports
item.description: The Ministry of Emergency Situations reported that children playing with fire caused a fatal fire in the 'Korkem-3' residential complex in Astana, which resulted in the deaths of three children. The fire originated inside the apartment. A criminal case was dropped due to insufficient evidence of a crime. The children's mother survived and was hospitalized with burns.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Reduce Overseas Medical Treatment for Children
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to increase access to high-tech medical treatments domestically, aiming to reduce the number of children sent abroad for procedures. The Ministry of Health reported that specialized care for infants with developmental defects is available regionally. Technologies like the 'Gamma Knife' and proton therapy are already in use, with plans to introduce radioiodine therapy and advanced vascular malformation treatment protocols.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Italy Sign Agreements Worth $436 Million
item.description: Kazakhstan and Italy have signed cooperation agreements totaling $436 million following a trade and economic mission in Rome. The agreements aim to expand mutual trade, facilitate direct product supplies, foster industrial cooperation, and implement joint projects. Special attention was given to increasing Kazakh agricultural exports, including grain and its processed products, and exploring food supply opportunities to Italian retail networks.

item.title: Taliban Official Claims Women's Rights Not Addressed in Doha Agreement
item.description: Shahabuddin Delawar, head of the Afghan Red Crescent Society under Taliban rule, stated that the Doha Agreement between the Taliban and the US did not mention women. Delawar, a former negotiator, asserted that the word "woman" is absent from the agreement's text. He attributed this to the conservative Pashtun culture regarding women.

item.title: Iranian Lawmaker Praises Afghanistan's Support, Accuses Pakistan of Hypocrisy
item.description: An Iranian lawmaker, Mohsen Zanganeh, praised Afghanistan's support for Iran during US-Iran tensions and criticized Pakistan's actions. Zanganeh claimed a post attributed to Pakistan's parliamentary speaker during Tehran-Washington negotiations was actually written by Americans. He labeled Pakistan's alleged conduct as "hypocrisy" and appreciated Afghan solidarity.

item.title: Investigative Journalist Bolot Temirov Receives International Award in London
item.description: Investigative journalist Bolot Temirov, whose work was declared extremist in Kyrgyzstan, has received the international award The Albies from the Clooney Foundation for Justice. The ceremony took place in London. Temirov's projects, Temirov Live and 'Ait, Ait dese', have been labeled extremist in Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: EU Appoints New Special Representative for Afghanistan
item.description: The European Union has appointed Danish diplomat Thomas Felsner as its new Special Representative for Afghanistan. Felsner stated that the people of Afghanistan, especially women and girls, will remain central to the EU's engagement. He succeeds Gilles Bertrand and previously worked in the EU's External Action Service and as head of the European Commission's political section in Moscow.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks Among World's 35 Most Influential Countries
item.description: Kazakhstan has secured the 34th position out of 100 countries in the 2026 Most Powerful Countries ranking by World Population Review. The nation ranks higher than the UAE, Norway, Saudi Arabia, and Iran. The ranking considers economic and political influence, international alliances, leadership potential, and military capabilities. Kazakhstan leads Central Asian nations in the well-being index.

item.title: Kazakhstan Farmers Seek Sunflower Import Ban Amid Record Harvest Expectations
item.description: Kazakh farmers are anticipating a record sunflower harvest and are proposing a ban on imports from Russia. They are concerned that cheap Russian sunflower oil could depress domestic prices, which are already showing signs of pressure. Experts suggest government intervention to prevent market disruption.

item.title: US Report: Taliban Continued Sexual Abuse of Children, Including 'Bacha Bazi'
item.description: The U.S. Department of State's 2026 report on human trafficking states the Taliban have not effectively combatted the issue and continued the sexual exploitation of boys, including 'bacha bazi.' The report notes no investigations or convictions for human trafficking, and a lack of victim identification or protection. Taliban restrictions hinder victim access to services.

item.title: French Experts Assess Kazakhstan's Role in Central Asian Modernization
item.description: French experts have positively evaluated Kazakhstan's ongoing political and legal reforms. Journalist Radouane Kuraq highlighted Kazakhstan as a model for strengthening the rule of law in Central Asia, citing reforms in parliamentary structure, judiciary, and human rights protection. Geopolitical advisor Sebastien Boussois noted Kazakhstan's significant regional position.

item.title: Astana Declaration on Digital Labor Signed at International Forum
item.description: An international forum in Astana concluded with the signing of the Astana Tripartite Declaration on Digital Labor and Artificial Intelligence. The forum, held in honor of World Day for Decent Work and Trade Union Day, also adopted a Digital Charter for Trade Unions. Discussions focused on developing digital labor market infrastructure and integrating modern technologies.

item.title: Two Workers Die During Water Pipe Replacement in Shymkent
item.description: Two workers have died while replacing water pipes in Shymkent. The incident occurred in a deep well where three employees of a private company were working. Preliminary reports suggest the young men, aged 20-22, may have died from gas poisoning. A criminal investigation has been launched.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Withhold Details of Military Accident Aid to Families
item.description: Kazakhstan will not disclose the amount of aid or personal data of military personnel killed or injured during exercises in the Caspian Sea. This decision was made at the request of relatives to protect privacy, according to Bekmurat Zhusupov, chairman of the Mangystau Public Council. All funds have been distributed according to established procedures.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks 34th in World Population Review's Most Powerful Countries Index
item.description: Kazakhstan has been ranked 34th in the World Population Review's 'Most Powerful Countries 2026' index, placing it between Hungary and Egypt. The ranking considers factors like leadership, economic and political influence, international alliances, and military power. Among post-Soviet states, only Russia ranked higher.

item.title: Doctor Arrested in Bukhara for Taking $500 for Medical Certificate
item.description: A doctor from a family polyclinic in Bukhara, Uzbekistan, has been arrested for allegedly accepting $500. The doctor reportedly promised to prepare a medical certificate for a citizen to obtain an academic leave from their educational institution. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Competition Committee investigates justification for mobile operator tariff increases
item.description: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee has launched an investigation into the justification for upcoming mobile operator tariff hikes. Consumers have complained about rising prices without guaranteed service quality, limited data usage, and non-transferable unused internet. The committee will take action if anti-competitive practices or consumer rights violations are found.
